newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's ruling party says no to NATO and WEU.
newsitem.headline: Austria's ruling party says no to NATO and WEU.

text.p: Austria's governing Social Democrats insisted on Friday they were opposed to joining any military alliance but said they remained committed to Austrian participation in international peace-keeping missions.
"Austria has no reason to join a military pact and to give up its neutrality for that purpose," the Social Democratic Party (SPOe) said in a strategy paper quoted by the Austrian news agency APA.

It quoted Chancellor Franz Vranitzky as saying his party was opposed to Austrian membership of either NATO or the WEU (Western European Union), the European Union's future defence arm, unless the political environment changed "substantially".
"Austria has reached the limit of its defence policy. We don't need to cross it," Vranitzky said.

The SPOe and its junior coalition partner, the conservative People's Party, have long been divided over whether Austria should give up its neutral status and become a member of a western military alliance.
Austria obtained observer status at the WEU after joining the European Union in January of last year.

Over the past 18 months the conservatives have increasingly backed modifying or ending neutrality, while the far-right Freedom Party has called for NATO membership. But the SPOe's position seems backed by a majority of Austrians with a recent poll showing just 23 percent of voters backing NATO membership.
Austria, straddling the former Cold War border between the feuding Eastern and Western blocs, has been neutral since 1955, when it drew up its post-World War Two constitution.

The Soviet Union, which occupied Austria after the war with allies Britain, France and the United States, demanded Austria enshrine neutrality as a pillar of its national charter before it agreed to withdraw troops.
A small contingent of Austrian troops is participating in the U.S.-led peacekeeping effort in Bosnia.
